SK2152 The path comparison assumes the file system's case rules

A path-valued string is compared with a hard-coded case-insensitive StringComparison, which is right on Windows and macOS and wrong on Linux.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

Two paths differing only in case are one file on Windows and on a default macOS volume, and two files on Linux. Folding them together on Linux is the failure a path comparison may never have — it serves one file's answer for another — and it is invisible on the developer's machine, appearing only in the container. ⚠ Skala's own answer to this is already in the tree and the rule is written from it: SarifWriter.PathComparison is OperatingSystem.IsLinux() ? StringComparison.Ordinal : StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase, and CacheKeyPathTests asserts the correct answer on all three platforms rather than skipping on two of them. So the guidance is not "stop ignoring case" — it is "compare the path the way this file system compares it", chosen at run time.

Example

Instead of:

if (Path.GetFullPath(a).Equals(b, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { }

Write:

static StringComparison PathComparison { get; } =
    OperatingSystem.IsLinux() ? StringComparison.Ordinal : StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase;

if (Path.GetFullPath(a).Equals(b, PathComparison)) { }

When it does not fire

⚠ An operand must be *provably* a path, and a name is not a proof. The finding requires that one side of the comparison is the result of a System.IO.Path member, or a FullName / DirectoryName / Name read from a System.IO.FileSystemInfo. A parameter called filePath is not enough: name-based path detection is how this kind of rule acquires its false positives, and the recall it costs is recall on code where the rule would be guessing. ⚠ Only a hard-coded case-*insensitive* constant is reported — OrdinalIgnoreCase, InvariantCultureIgnoreCase, CurrentCultureIgnoreCase. The Ordinal direction is wrong on Windows for the same reason, but reporting it would fire on every correct comparison written by someone targeting Linux only, and there is no signal in the source that separates the two. A comparison passed a non-constant StringComparison — a field, a property, a parameter — is already the shape this rule asks for and is silent. ⚠ `hasFix: false`: the repair is to introduce a platform-dependent comparison value, which is a new declaration somewhere the analyzer cannot choose, and the framework offers no built-in to point at.
